Align roof trim panel
 at front of vehicle over inside visor mounting 
holes and secure.

 as a guide when centering sliding roof panel headlining retainer (52124)
.

 so that seam is centered at

.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Mouldings, Exterior

 Side Sill 

 Removal 

 NOTE: Refer to the illustrations following this procedure while performing the following steps.

Remove screw securing front side member moulding to inner surface of front wheel well. 

Remove pushpins securing moulding to lower inner edge of rocker panel. 

 NOTE: Some retainers will pull out of the moulding downstanding flange and remain in the sheet metal holes. Use pliers to 
peel-out retainers. The moulding downstanding flange will be damaged. Removed mouldings and retainers cannot be reused. Install 

a 
new moulding to the vehicle. 

Grab moulding at front wheel well and pull moulding away from vehicle to disengage upper retainers. 

Grab moulding at rear wheel well and pull moulding away from vehicle to disengage upper retainers. 

 Installation 

Install moulding to vehicle by aligning 17 upper arrowhead retainers to 17 holes in sheet metal and engage retainers. Be 
sure to engage fingers between front and rear moulding.

To make sure of full engagement of the upper arrowhead retainers, apply hand pressure between every two retainers. 

Install pushpins to lower inner edge of rocker panel.

Install screw retaining moulding to front wheel well and tighten to 0.9-1.3 Nm (8-11 lb-in).

 Roof�Ditch Moulding 

 Removal 

 CAUTION: Take care not to damage the surrounding paintwork. 

 NOTE: Moulding (517C44) will be damaged upon removal and must be replaced. 

Carefully pry the end of moulding
 away from the groove and then pull the remainder along 
its length. 

All of the adhesive tape will not come off with the moulding. Small pieces of tape can be removed from the moulding 
groove in roof by rolling with your thumb across the sheet metal surface or by using 3M® Scotch-Brite® Moulding 

Adhesive Stripe Removal Disc, 3M® Part No. 07501 or 07502. 

[FIGURE: R10928C.gif]

 Installation 

When all tape is removed, wipe area with isopropyl alcohol and clean soft cloth. Make sure that all tape residue and road 

dirt is removed. A clean surface is required for application of new mouldings.

If paint surface is damaged during removal of mouldings, service as required.

 NOTE: Mouldings should not be installed on vehicle unless sheet metal surface temperatures exceed 27°C (80°F) and the 
moulding is at 21°C (70°F) minimum.

Be sure the moulding is lined up correctly; once the tape sticks, the moulding cannot be removed.

Remove vinyl liner from new moulding. Do not touch or contaminate adhesive surface of moulding. 

Tuck front end of the moulding under the windshield seal and position the moulding fore-aft flush to roof/bodyside 
vertical wall. 

Push moulding into ditch (slowly working from windshield to backlite). Make sure moulding goes straight down and does not 

rotate while being pushed to bottom of ditch. 

Tuck the rear end of the moulding under the backlite seal. 

Press the moulding in with a hand roller, applying a minimum of 138 
kPa (20 psi) pressure to make sure of proper adhesion.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Luggage Carrier�Roof

 Rails and Slats 

 Removal 

For roof luggage carrier side rail, remove six screws per side and loosen two screws on roof luggage carrier side rail. 

For roof luggage carrier slats, drill out five rivets at each slat. 

 Installation 

 NOTE: Center rivet on each luggage carrier slat is a fore-aft locator and it must be installed before remaining rivets. 

For roof luggage carrier slats, position on vehicle roof panel (50200)
 after applying sealer around rivet holes. Install rivet 
into place. 

For roof luggage carrier side rails, position on vehicle roof panel
 after applying sealer around holes. Install eight screws. Tighten to 2.7-3.7 Nm (24-32 lb-in).

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Mirror, Outside Rear View

 Power 

Electrically-powered outside rear view mirrors (17682)
 are standard (heated outside rear view mirror is optional). The heating function of outside rear view mirrors
 operates as follows: 

Activates when heated back window switch is turned on. This is indicated by the back window switch light.

The heating element will remain on for ten minutes. Timing is controlled by the generic electronic module (GEM). 

The outside rear view mirror control (17B676)
: 

is located on the front door trim panel (23942)
. 

operates both outside rear view mirrors
. 

is designed to tilt the outside rear view mirror
 up, down, left or right by pressing knob in 
the desired direction. 

Move the switch on the outside rear view mirror control
 to the LH or RH position to 
select the outside rear view mirror
 requiring adjustment.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Mirror, Inside Rear View

 Manual 

The inside rear view mirror (17700)
:

consists of a mirror and housing assembly that: 

mounts to an inside rear view mirror bracket (17698)
 at the upper center of the windshield glass (03100)
. 

The inside rear view mirror bracket
 is glued to the windshield glass
 with a two-part epoxy.

can be adjusted in any direction. 

can be changed from a day to a night position to reduce the glare from the headlamps of vehicles in the rear.

move the tab toward you for the night position and away from you for the day position. 

has a swivel bracket that lets the inside rear view mirror
 move up or down and from side to side.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Mirrors, Rear View

Refer to Electrical and Vacuum Troubleshooting Manual, Cell 124 , Power Mirrors for schematic and connector information. 

Refer to Electrical and Vacuum Troubleshooting Manual, Cell 56 , Rear Window Defrost/Heated Mirrors for schematic and connector information. 

 Inspection and Verification 

Verify the customer's concern by operating the outside rear view mirrors (17682)
 to duplicate the condition

Inspect the components to determine if any of the following mechanical or electrical conditions are present:

 VISUAL INSPECTION CHART

Mechanical

Electrical

Damaged outside rear view mirrors

Damaged outside rear view mirror control

Open fuse, fuse junction panel

Fuse 22 (5A)

Fuse 32 (5A)

Fuse 5 (5A)

Damaged heated back window relay

Damage to wiring harness

Loose or corroded connections

If the inspection reveals obvious concerns that can be readily identified, service as required. 

If the concerns remain after the inspection, determine the symptoms and go to the Symptom Chart.

 Symptom Chart 

Refer to the Electrical and Vacuum Troubleshooting Manual for connector numbers cited in the pinpoint tests.

Use Rotunda Digital Volt-Ohmmeter 418-F164 (014-00407) or equivalent to perform pinpoint tests.

 Glass, Outside Mirror 

[FIGURE: AN0324B.gif]

 Removal 

 NOTE: The outside rear view mirror glass (17K707)
 and case is attached using snap 
tabs. It is not necessary to break the outside rear view mirror glass
 to remove. 

Position inboard edge of outside rear view mirror glass
 inward to give maximum clearance at 
the outboard edge of outside rear view mirror glass
. 

With fingertips, pry bottom outboard corner of outside rear view mirror glass
 out of mirror housing until the 
snap tabs disengage. 

Disconnect two heater element wiring connectors. 

Remove outside rear view mirror glass
 from vehicle. 

 Installation 

Connect two heater element electrical connectors. 

Position outside rear view mirror glass
 and case over power actuator motor 
using locator tabs and fingers. 

Press evenly in the center of the outside rear view mirror glass
 and case until the snap tabs 
engage. 

Apply pressure around the outside rear view mirror glass
 and case area to ensure snap 
engagement. 

Clean outside rear view mirror glass
 and mirror housing with Ultra-Clear Spray Glass Cleaner E4AZ-19C507-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M14P5-A.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Mirror Bracket, Inside Rear View

 Removal 

Remove inside rear view mirror (17700)
 as described. Mark location of inside rear view mirror bracket (17698)
 on outside of windshield glass (03100)
. 

Apply low heat from Rotunda Master Heat Gun 107-R0301 or equivalent until the vinyl softens. Peel inside rear view mirror bracket
 off the windshield glass
. 

[FIGURE: N12639A.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

03100

Inside Rear View Mirror

 Installation 

Make sure windshield glass
, inside rear view mirror bracket
 and adhesive kit (Rearview Mirror Adhesive D9AZ-19554-CA or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESB-M2G176-A) are at least 
at room temperature: 18°C 
(65.4°F). 

If windshield glass
 is being replaced, locate and mark inside rear view mirror bracket
 location on the outside surface of windshield glass
.

Thoroughly clean bonding surfaces of windshield glass
 and inside rear view mirror bracket
 to remove old adhesive. Use mild abrasive cleaner on windshield glass
 and fine sandpaper on inside rear view mirror bracket
 to lightly roughen surface. Wipe clean with alcohol-moistened cloth. 

Crush accelerator vial (part of Rearview Mirror Adhesive D9AZ-19554-CA or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESB-M2G176-A) and apply accelerator to bonding surface of inside rear view mirror bracket
 and windshield glass
. Let dry for three minutes. 

Apply two drops of Rearview Mirror Adhesive D9AZ-19554-CA or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESB-M2G176-A to the 
mounting surface of the inside rear view mirror bracket
. Using a clean toothpick or wooden match, quickly spread the adhesive evenly over the mounting surface of the inside rear view mirror bracket
. 

Quickly position the inside rear view mirror bracket
 on the windshield glass
. Press the inside rear view mirror bracket
 firmly against the windshield glass
 for one minute. 

Allow bond to set for five minutes. Remove any excess bonding material from the windshield glass
 with an alcohol-moistened cloth. After bond has set re-install inside rear view mirror
.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Mirrors, Outside

 CAUTION: Outside rear view mirrors (17682) should not be cleaned with a dry cloth or abrasive cleaning powders. Do not remove ice with a scraper. The outside rear view mirror glass (17K707)
 should only be cleaned with a soft, clean cloth and mild detergent and water or Ultra-Clear Spray Glass Cleaner E4AZ-19C507-AA 

or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESR-M14P5-A, otherwise damage to the reflective surface may result.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Seat Tracks, Manual

Thefront seat track (61704)
 contains the following features: 

Thefront seat cushion extension handle (603A86)
 is located at the front of 
the seat. 

Pulling thefront seat cushion extension handle
allows forward or rearward 
movement of the front seat assembly. 

Manualfront seat tracks
 are retained to the front floor pan (11135)
 as follows:

Studs with nut and washer assemblies are at both rear positions.

A flange head bolt is used on both front positions.

Nuts and bolts retaining the front seat tracks
 are removed from inside the vehicle.

 andfront seat back head restraint (611A08)
as described.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Seats, Front

 Power, Six-Way 

The six-way power seat system contains the following features:

a rack and pinon-type drive for seat adjustment

horizontal, vertical and tilt adjustments

a reversibleseat regulator motor (14547)
, seat regulator control switch (14A701)
, vertical rack and pinon and horizontal rack and pinon drives

the mechanical portion of thefront seat track (61704)
 in the horizontal drive consists of a rack and 
pinion drive on each track with a transmission on the inboard side

The front armature and the horizontal drive units are activated when theseat regulator control switch
 is actuated.

The seat moves forward or rearward by means of the rack mounted to the lower track traveling through the pinon and 
transmission housing on each upper track.

The seat regulator motor
 and transmission are serviced only by replacing 
the entire front seat track
.

Theseat regulator control switch
 is serviced separately.

 Circuit Protection 

The power seat circuit is protected by Fuse 6 POWER SEATS (30A) in the power distribution box.

Section 01-10: Seats and Tracks

1998 Taurus, Sable Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Recliner

 Manual 

The front seat back latch system contains the following features:

The reclining seat back is adjusted by a front seat back latch (62648)
 on the outboard side of the seat cushion.

The seat back reclines when the latch is pulled and lifted upward, the seat back is pushed to the desired position and 
the latch is released.

The seat back returns to its full-up position with spring action when the latch is lifted and occupant back pressure is 
removed.

The entire front seat back latch
 must be replaced if any component is non-functional or damaged. It is a modular design and components cannot be serviced or 
replaced individually.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Lumbar Support System

The lumbar support system includes the following components:

seat control switch (14C715)

front seat back pad adjuster (65500)

front seat back pad adjusting pump (65530)

related wiring harness andfront seat back pad adjusting tube (65512)

All components are located at or under thefront seat cushion frame and spring (63100)
except for thefront seat back pad adjuster
 and mechanical system.

During inflate mode, the front seat back pad adjusting pump
 pumps air through a front seat back pad adjusting tube
 to the seat back control switch and housing check valve.

Air is routed through afront seat back pad adjusting tube
 to the front seat back pad 
adjuster bags located in the seat back.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Seat Control Switch

 CAUTION: The longer nipple on the seat control switch (14C715)
 (located at the center of the switch body) should always be connected to the front seat back pad adjusting hose leading to thefront seat back pad adjuster (65500)
. The shorter nipple on the switch body connects to the front seat back pad adjusting pump outlet. If this order is reversed, 
the front seat back pad adjuster
 will not hold air pressure. 

The seat control switch
 performs three functions: 

activates front seat back pad adjusting pump (65530)
.

acts as a one-way check valve for air passage to front seat back pad adjuster
. Once inflated, the seat control switch
 is returned to its normal mode and the check valve closes. This maintains air pressure in the front seat back pad adjuster
. 

When deflated, the check valve opens to deflate the front seat back pad adjuster
. In this mode, the front seat back pad adjusting pump
 does not operate.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Seat, Rear

 Fold Down Rear � Sedan 

 WARNING: IF THE REAR SEAT BACK IS NOT SECURELY LATCHED, PASSENGERS OR OBJECTS COULD BE THROWN AND INJURY COULD OCCUR IN THE EVENT 
OF A SUDDEN STOP OR COLLISION. 

The fold-down rear seat backs are split (60/40) and operate independently of each other. On some models, the rear seat 
back also incorporates a fold-down armrest. The rear seat backs operate in the following manner:

Pull up on straps, located on the inboard sides of the rear seat back, to release the seat and hold down to the cargo 
position.

To return the seat to the seating position, raise the seat back to the upright position and make sure seat back latches 
into position.

 Fold Down Rear�Station Wagon 

 WARNING: IF THE SECOND SEAT BACK OR OPTIONAL THIRD SEAT BACK IS NOT SECURELY LATCHED, PASSENGERS OR OBJECTS COULD BE THROWN AND 
INJURY COULD OCCUR IN THE EVENT OF A SUDDEN STOP OR COLLISION. 

The fold-down seat backs on the second seat, which are split (60/40) and operate independently of each other, operate in 
the following manner:

Pull up on the release handle located on the top outboard corner of the seat back to fold a seat back to the cargo 
position.

To return seat back to the upright (seating) position, raise the seat back to the normal upright position and make sure 
the seat back is latched in the upright position.

 Child Seat, Integral 

 Station Wagon 

The station wagon second seat has an optional integrated child seat. The integrated child seat includes:

seat back frame

seat pad and cover

fold-down latching system

The integral child seat maintains full seat back fold-down capability and is equipped with a latch interlock system. The 
seatback cannot be folded unless the child seat is closed. The child seat may not be deployed unless the seatback is latched.

Seats and Tracks

 Inspection and Verification 

Verify the customer's original concern by operating the power seat(s) to duplicate the concern.

Inspect to determine if one of the following mechanical or electrical concerns apply:

 VISUAL INSPECTION CHART

Mechanical

Electrical

Seat tracks obstructed.

Seat at limit(s) of travel.

Damaged front seat back pad adjusting tube
.

Damaged seat control switch
and valve.

Open power distribution box Fuse 6 power seats, 30A.

Loose, corroded or damaged connectors.

Damaged switches.

Damaged motors.

If the inspection reveals obvious concern(s) that can be readily identified, service as required.

If the concern(s) remains after the inspection, determine the symptom(s) and go to the Symptom Chart.

 Removal

Remove rear seat back side pads (66878)
 by removing retaining screws (one each).

.

 NOTE: On integrated child seat, pivot pin and lower latch pin must be aligned during installation.

 in the folded forward position, align the 
keys on the pin with the keyway on the seat back frame.

 NOTE: A nut and bolt have been provided on the LH (40 percent) rear seat back release latch
 only, to align the RH seat back to the fixed position (± 2 degrees adjustment). To align the RH seat back, loosen the 
nut and bolt and reposition the bolt in 
its slot. Tighten the bolt and nut to 39-51 Nm (29-37 lb-ft). Make sure seat backs operate properly after alignment.

Check rear seat back release latch
 for proper operation. 

Install rear seat back side pads
 and retaining screws.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Head Restraints

 Removal 

Unscrew front seat head rest guide rod retainers (610A18)
. 

Pull up on front seat back head restraint (611A08)
. Compress foam in area of front seat head rest guide rod sleeves (610A16)
. 

Remove front seat back head restraint positioning springs. Pull front seat back head restraint

up and out. 

 Installation 

Slide front seat head rest guide rod retainers
onto front seat back 
head restraint posts. 

Compress foam in front seat head rest guide rod sleeve area. Install
positioning springs on front seat head rest guide rod sleeves
. 

Insert front seat back head restraint posts (notches on posts facing
rearward) into front seat head rest guide rod sleeves
and push down to engage 
positioning spring. 

 NOTE: Front seat back head restraint must operate smoothly throughout its range of travel, must remain in any fixed position, and must not be freely removable from 

the seat back. If any of these 
conditions are not met, check for proper installation of positioning spring onto front seat head rest guide rod sleeve
. 

Tighten front seat head rest guide rod retainers
onto front seat head rest guide rod sleeves
. 

Adjust front seat back head restraint
 by applying hand pressure, either up 
or down, to center area of front seat back head restraint
.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Armrest, Front Seat Center

 Disassembly 

Carefully pull up on armrest pivot bolt covers (one on each side).

Remove two pivot bolts (one each side) from armrest mounting bracket.

Apply pressure inward on armrest to disengage two pivot plate pins from armrest mounting bracket.

Pull up on armrest to disengage opposite side and remove armrest from console. 

From under console, remove two screws retaining bolster to console.

Disengage tabs retaining bolster to console and remove bolster.

Remove two cup holder rubber liners.

Remove two screws - one in each cup holder.

Cassette storage equipped - Remove two screw covers and remove two screws. Phone storage equipped - Remove two screws 
from phone receiver and remove receiver. Remove one screw cover and remove one screw.

Lift drink tray and disconnect phone cable from phone storage compartment (if equipped).

Remove cup holder, cassette and/or phone storage assembly from console.

Remove ash receptacle.

Remove two screws and ash receptacle housing from console.

 Assembly 

To assemble, transfer armrest pivot plates to new armrest and reverse Disassembly procedure.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Latch, Manual

The front seat back latch (62648)
 is modular and does not require adjustments. 
However, proper lubrication of a hesitant front seat back latch
 is permitted using Multi-Purpose Grease D0AZ-19584-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESB-M1C93-B. 

The only authorized service permitted on the front seat back latch
is the following: 

Tightening of all retaining screws as described. 

Replacement (in entirety) of a damaged or non-functional front seat back latch
.

Removal of any foreign material, such as tie straps, pieces of foam and trim.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Accessory Delay

The accessory delay is designed to supply power to the power window system after the ignition switch is turned to the OFF position for up to 45 seconds.

The accessory delay system operates in the following manner:

When the generic electronic module (GEM) senses that the ignition switch has been turned OFF, GEM starts two timing functions:

accessory delay system 

battery saver system

The GEM supplies a ground signal to relays for both systems.

Ground input to the battery saver relay supplies power to the accessory delay relay.

Ground input to the accessory delay relay supplies power to the accessory delay system. 

The GEM will shut down the accessory delay system after 45 seconds and shut down the battery saver system after 40 minutes.

The accessory delay time out will be cancelled if either front door is opened or ignition switch is turned to RUN/ACC/START.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Window, One-Touch Down

The driver's window regulator control switch (14529)
 has a one-touch down feature which allows:

the front door window glass (21410)
 to fully lower by pressing the LH front
 window regulator control switch
to activate the front door window glass
.

the front door window glass
 to stop while it is moving downward by pressing
 window regulator control switch
to activate the front door window glass
 in
 either the up or down direction.

the front door window glass
 to operate without the one-touch down feature when the
 window regulator control switch
 is held down for more than one-half second and the button is released, which will activate the
 front door window glass
.

When the window regulator control switch
 is held down for 0.06-0.32 seconds the GEM will ground the one-touch down relay coil and
 front door window glass
 will move to its full down position.

The one-touch down feature can be cancelled by any of the following actions:

GEM times out 6.9 seconds

pushing either side of the LH front window regulator control switch

GEM detects a stall condition at its current sense inputs

accessory delay system time out

Section 01-11: Glass, Frames and Mechanisms

1998 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Switch and Light, Heated Back Window

The heated back window switch:

is an integral part of the integrated control panel.

sends a momentary ground signal to the generic electronic module (GEM) when activated.

GEM then sends a ground signal to the heated back window relay, supplying power to the heated back window grid and heated side mirrors.

GEM starts the 10 minute time-out function. At the end of 10 minutes, the GEM will discontinue the ground supply to the heated back window relay. A second press of the
 heated back window switch and light (18C621)
 during these 10 minutes will cause GEM to discontinue ground signal to heated back window relay, turning the system OFF.

If the GEM time-out function has started with ignition switch in ACC, and the ignition switch is turned to START the GEM timing is interrupted and will resume when ignition switch is turned to RUN.

Turning the ignition switch OFF will cancel GEM time-out function.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Glass, Frames and Mechanisms

 Inspection and Verification 

Verify the customer concern by operating the power windows/heated back window to duplicate the condition.

Inspect the components of the power window system to determine if any of the following mechanical or electrical concerns apply.

 VISUAL INSPECTION CHART

Mechanical

Electrical

Window alignment.

Window mounting (regulator and bracket).

Window frame interference.

Open power distribution box Fuse 4 (30A) and 7 (40A).

Fuse junction panel Fuse 23 (5A), 33 (5A), 12 (5A) and 32 (5A).

Damage to wiring harness.

Loose or corroded connections.

Damaged switches.

Damaged relays in fuse junction panel.

Damaged back window grid wires.

If inspection reveals obvious concern that can be readily identified, serviced as required.

If the concern remains after the inspection, connect the Rotunda New Generation STAR (NGS) Tester 418-F048 (007-00500) or equivalent to the data link connector (DLC) located beneath the instrument panel, turn the ignition switch to RUN and
 select the vehicle to be tested from the NGS menu. If the NGS does not communicate with the vehicle:

check that program card is properly installed.

check connections to vehicle.

check ignition switch position.

If the NGS still does not communicate with the vehicle, refer to the New Generation STAR (NGS) Tester manual.

Perform DATA LINK DIAGNOSTICS TEST using the NGS. If the NGS responds with:

CKT 70 = ALL MODULE NO RESP/NOT EQUIP, go to Communication System Diagnostics in Section 18-04 to diagnose network concern.

NO RESPONSE/NOT EQUIPPED for Generic Electronic Module (GEM), go to Pinpoint Test B.

If the GEM is not listed for a communication concern execute Self Test Diagnostics for the GEM.

If DTCs retrieved are related to the concern, go to the Generic Electronic Module (GEM) Diagnostic Trouble Code (DTC) Index to continue diagnostics.

If no DTCs related to the concern are retrieved, go to the Symptom Chart to continue diagnostics.

Rotunda Service Bay Diagnostic System (SBDS®) 418-F001 (001-00001) may also be used to diagnose this system.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Windshield Glass

 Removal 

 WARNING: SAFETY GLASSES AND GLOVES MUST BE WORN. FAILURE TO DO SO MAY RESULT IN PERSONAL INJURY. 

Remove windshield wiper arms and blades. Refer to Section 01-16 .

Remove visors and drop headliner near windshield opening down to avoid cutting headliner during windshield glass removal. Place a small block of suitable material between headliner and roof to act as a spacer. Remove interior garnish mouldings
 as required.

Remove cowl vent screen (018A16)
. Refer to Section 01-02 .

Remove inside rear view mirror (17700)
. Refer to Section 01-09 .

 CAUTION: Use care to avoid damage to the instrument panel. 

Use Rotunda Knife with Offset Blade 107-R1511 Rotunda Interior Auto-Glass Cut-Out Knife Kit 164-R2450 or equivalent to cut adhesive. Refer to manufacturer's instructions when using tool. 

 Rotunda Knife with Offset Blade 

[FIGURE: N6999C.gif]

 Rotunda Interior Auto-Glass Cut-Out Knife 

[FIGURE: N9628C.gif]

Remove windshield glass (03100)
 and moulding assemblies from vehicle.

 NOTE: Care should be taken to avoid scratching the paint.

Clean dirt and debris from area around urethane, then trim remaining urethane on pinch weld to within 1 to 1.5 mm (0.04 to 0.06 inch) thickness with utility knife or razor blade. When completed, surface should be smooth and free of cuts
 and contamination. 

[FIGURE: N10128A.gif]

Check pinch weld sealing area for damaged sheet metal, rust or foreign objects which may have caused, or may cause, glass breakage. Service metal if necessary. 

 Installation 

 NOTE: A minimum of 10 minutes is required for primer surface to dry. 

If painted sheet metal has been exposed anywhere along the flange, use the supplied wool applicator and apply Urethane Rubber Primer WSB-M2G234-C or equivalent to windshield pinch weld.

Place windshield and moulding assembly on a low, stable work surface, inside up. 

Clean windshield glass
 with non-alcohol-based glass cleaner.

 NOTE: Wipe off Urethane Glass Cleaner WSB-M5B280-C2 or equivalent immediately after application because it flash-dries. Prep application must be applied twice.

Using a clean wool applicator, wipe inside glass edge with Urethane Glass Cleaner WSB-M5B280-C2 or equivalent 21 mm (0.8 inch) wide along top and sides, 70 mm (2.75 inch) wide along bottom. Wipe off glass wipe and repeat prep application.

Properly align windshield glass
 to body. 

Make sure windshield glass stops (03296)
 are in place at bottom of windshield glass opening. Place
 windshield glass
 into opening. Center it top and bottom, side to side.

Using masking tape or crayon, make alignment marks at points on four sides of both windshield glass
 and window opening. 

Remove windshield glass
 and moulding assemblies from vehicle and place it back on work table. 

Thoroughly shake and stir Urethane Glass Primer WSB-M2G314-B or equivalent to make sure of uniform pigment mixing. 

 NOTE: Allow a minimum of five minutes for glass primer to dry.

Using a clean wool applicator, apply primer to inside glass edge 21 mm (0.8 inch) wide along top and sides and 70 mm (2.75 inch) wide along bottom.

[FIGURE: AN0643A.gif]

 NOTE: Leave a door window slightly open until adhesive is cured.

 NOTE: Apply new urethane on top of existing material on pinch weld.

Apply an even bead of Urethane Adhesive WSB-M2G316-B or equivalent around entire sheet metal pinch weld next to windshield moulding retaining leg. The bead should be triangular in shape, 16 mm (0.625 inch) high and 8 mm (0.33 inch) at base.
 Apply a double bead of urethane along the cowl top and the bottom of windshield opening. 

Install windshield glass
 onto vehicle, taking care to align marks on
 windshield glass
 to marks on body. This must be done before adhesive skins over.

Remove spacer and install headliner, windshield wiper arms, blades, visors and interior garnish moulding. Refer to Section 01-02 .

Install inside rear view mirror
. Refer to Section 01-09 .

 CAUTION: Use only urethane for service of air and water leaks in urethane-set windshield. 

 CAUTION: When replacing urethane installed glass parts, do not drive the vehicle until the urethane has cured. At temperatures above 21°C (70°F) and relative humidities above 50%, adequate cure time is typically 24 hours (less at
 higher temperatures and higher humidities). See detailed instructions provided by the urethane manufacturer. Inadequate or improper curing can adversely affect the retention of the windshield. 

Check installation for air and water leaks in urethane seal.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Back Window Glass

 Removal 

 WARNING: SAFETY GLASSES AND GLOVES MUST BE WORN. FAILURE TO DO SO MAY RESULT IN PERSONAL INJURY. 

Disconnect rear window defroster wires.

Remove interior garnish mouldings and drop headliner near back window to avoid cutting headliner during back window removal. Place a small block of suitable material between headliner and roof to act as a spacer. 

 CAUTION: Use care to avoid damage to the rear package tray cover panel. 

Use Rotunda Knife with Offset Blade 107-R1511 and Rotunda Interior Auto-Glass Cut-Out Knife Kit 164-R2450 or equivalent to cut sealer. Refer to manufacturer's instructions when using tool. 

 Rotunda Knife with Offset Blade 

[FIGURE: N6999C.gif]

 Rotunda Interior Auto-Glass Cut-Out Knife 

[FIGURE: N9628C.gif]

Remove back window glass (42006)
 from vehicle.

Clean around pinch weld area to remove any dirt and debris that could contaminate the existing urethane once it is trimmed.

Trim remaining urethane on pinch weld to within 1 and 2.0 mm (0.04 and 0.08 inch) thickness with utility knife or razor blade. When completed, surface should be smooth and free of cuts and contamination. 

[FIGURE: N10128A.gif]

 NOTE: Use extreme care not to scratch or otherwise damage the pinch weld with tools to avoid rust formation.

Check pinch weld sealing area for damaged sheet metal, rust or foreign objects which may have caused, or may cause, glass breakage. Service metal if necessary. 

 Installation 

 NOTE: A minimum of 10 minutes is required for primer surface to dry. 

If painted sheet metal has been exposed or damaged anywhere along the pinch weld, use the supplied wool applicator and apply Urethane Rubber Primer WSB-M2G234-C or equivalent to rear window pinch weld.

Place on a low, stable work surface, inside up. 

Clean back window glass
 with non-alcohol-based glass cleaner.

 NOTE: Wipe off Urethane Glass Cleaner WSB-M5B280-C2 or equivalent immediately after application because it flash-dries. Prep application must be applied twice.

Using a clean wool applicator, wipe inside glass edge with Urethane Glass Cleaner WSB-M5B280-C2 21 mm (0.8 inch) wide along top and sides, 30 mm (1.2 inch) wide along bottom. Wipe off glass wipe and repeat application.

[FIGURE: AN0643A.gif]

Properly align back window glass
 to body: 

Place back window glass
 into opening. Center it top and bottom, side to side.

Using masking tape or crayon, make alignment marks at points on four sides of both back window glass
 and window opening. 

Remove back window glass
 from vehicle and place it back on work table. 

Thoroughly shake and stir Urethane Glass Cleaner WSB-M2G314-B or equivalent to make sure of uniform pigment mixing. 

 NOTE: Allow a minimum of five minutes for glass primer to dry.

Using a clean wool applicator, apply primer to inside glass edge 21 mm (0.8 inch) wide along top and sides and 30 mm (1.2 inch) wide along bottom.

 NOTE: Leave a door window slightly open until adhesive is cured.

Apply an even bead of Urethane Adhesive WSB-M2G316-B or equivalent around entire sheet metal flange on top of existing bead of urethane. The bead should be triangular in shape, 16 mm (0.625 inch) high and 8 mm (0.33 inch) at base. 

 CAUTION: When replacing urethane installed glass parts, do not drive the vehicle until the urethane has cured. At temperatures above 21°C (70°F) and relative humidities above 50%, adequate cure time is typically 24 hours (less at
 higher temperatures and higher humidities). See detailed instructions provided by the urethane manufacturer. Inadequate or improper curing can adversely affect the retention of the windshield. 

Install back window glass
 onto vehicle, taking care to align marks on glass to body. This must be done before adhesive skins over.

Reconnect rear window defroster wires.

Remove spacer and install headliner. Install all garnish mouldings. 

 CAUTION: Use only urethane for service of air and water leaks in urethane set back windows. 

Check installation for air and water leaks in urethane seal.

Window Regulator Electric Drive

 Removal 

Raise window glass to full-up position if possible. If glass cannot be raised and is in a partially down or full-down position, it must be supported so that it will not fall into door well when removing
 window regulator electric drive (23394)
.

.

 WARNING: IF THE FRONT DOOR POWER WINDOW REGULATOR COUNTERBALANCE SPRING MUST BE REMOVED OR REPLACED FOR ANY REASON, MAKE SURE THAT THE FRONT DOOR POWER WINDOW REGULATOR ARMS ARE IN A FIXED POSITION PRIOR TO REMOVAL TO PREVENT POSSIBLE INJURY
 DURING C-SPRING UNWIND. 

Remove three window regulator electric drive mounting screws. 

Remove window regulator electric drive
.

 Installation 

Position the window regulator electric drive
 to the power window regulator. Install the three screws snugly but do not tighten all the way.

Connect the window regulator electric drive wires at the connector and cycle the door window glass to make sure gear engagement. After the gears are engaged, tighten the three window regulator electric drive retaining screws to 6-10
 Nm (54-88 lb-in). 

Connect battery ground cable
. 

Check power window for proper operation. Install door trim panel and watershield. Refer to Section 01-05 .

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Door Glass Top Run

 Front 

 Removal 

 CAUTION: Removal of the front door glass top run (21596)
 is recommended only if damage occurs to the
 front door glass top run
. Due to the fragile make-up of the component, unnecessary removal may cause damage or breaks in the light-gauge steel carrier insert
 within the rubber seal of the front door glass top run
. 

Remove the following window glass components as described: 

front door belt line outside weatherstrip (21452) and
 front door belt line inside weatherstrip (21456)

two front door glass top run retainer screws

front door window glass (21410)

 CAUTION: The front door glass top run
 requires very CRITICAL AND SPECIAL HANDLING. The
 front door glass top run
 must be handled by the center section only�never from front or rear legs. The
 front door glass top runs
 must be handled in a manner that prevents damage to the A- and B-pillar corners. 

Removal of the door glass run may cause the retaining pins to break. Verify broken pins do not rattle in door.

To remove front door glass top run
, carefully pull
 front door glass top run
 off window opening pinch weld and remove through window opening. 

 Installation 

Insert the front leg of front door glass top run
. After the front (A-pillar section) and the rear (B-pillar section) of the
 front door glass top run
 is inserted into the front door (20124)
, locate
 moulded B-pillar corner of front door glass top run
 from pinch weld flange to upper corner of door frame. 

Apply hand pressure to front door glass top run
 from belt line area of B-pillar and push
 front door glass top run
 upward (vertically) into corner. Make sure
 front door glass top run
 is fully flush with sheet metal. 

While applying upward pressure along B-pillar, install front door glass top run
 onto door frame along B-pillar starting from top and moving downward. Use
 hand pressure to make sure front door glass top run
 is flush with outer door panel sheet metal. 

Use hand pressure from center of upper door frame area. Push front door glass top run
 rearward along pinch weld flange into B-pillar upper corner. Make
 sure front door glass top run
 is flush with outer door panel sheet metal at corner. 

While applying hand pressure rearward, install front door glass top run
 onto door frame pinch weld along upper door frame starting from B-pillar and going
 to A-pillar. 

Use hand pressure from lower A-pillar leg of front door glass top run
 and push
 front door glass top run
 upward (vertically) into corner. Make sure
 front door glass top run
 is fully flush with outside sheet metal. 

While applying upward hand pressure along A-pillar, install front door glass top run
 onto door frame. Use hand pressure to fully seat
 front door glass top run
. Make sure front door glass top run leg is fully seated. 

Install front door glass top run
 to door inner panel with two screws. Tighten to 7-10 Nm (62-88 lb-in).

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Grid Wire, Back Window Glass�Method I

Any break in the grid longer than 25 mm (1 inch) cannot be serviced. The back window glass (42006)
 must be replaced. For breaks less than 25 mm (1 inch) long, use
 the following procedure: 

 NOTE: If the first layer of the heated back window grid (brown) is damaged or missing, it will be necessary to apply brown Touch-Up Exterior Paint (Brush-in-Tube) AL81-5477-C or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M2P100-C on the
 back window glass
 prior to applying the Rear Window Defroster Repair D8AZ-19562-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESB-M4J58-A.

 Surface Preparation 

Bring the vehicle inside and warm it to 16°C (60°F) or above. 

 CAUTION: Do not use scrapers, sharp instruments or abrasive cleaners on the interior surface of the back window glass
 as this may cause damage to grid lines. 

Clean entire grid line repair area with Ultra-Clear Spray Glass Cleaner E4AZ-19C507-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M14P5-A to remove all dirt, wax, grease, oil or other foreign matter. It is important that repair area be
 clean and dry. 

 Mixing 

The bottle of Rear Window Defroster Repair D8AZ-19562-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESB-M4J58-A and touch-up paint must be at room temperature. Shake bottle for at least one minute for thorough mixing. Shake frequently during use.

 Application 

Mark location of break on outside of back window glass
. 

Using cellulose tape, mask off area directly above and below grid break. The break area should be at the center of the mask and tape gap must be no wider than existing grid line. 

[FIGURE: K3787E.gif]

 NOTE: If the brown layer of the grid is not broken or missing, apply only Rear Window Defroster Repair D8AZ-19562-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESB-M4J58-A to the break. 

Apply the repair coating in several smooth, continuous strokes (allowing three to five minutes drying time between coats) across the break area using the brush applicator in the cap. Extend the service coating at least 6.35 mm (1/4 inch) on
 both sides of the break area. 

If both brown and silver layers of grid are broken or missing, apply a coating of the dark walnut metallic Touch-Up Exterior Paint (Brush-in-Tube) AL81-5858-B or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M2P100-C across break area first. Two
 coats may be necessary to obtain proper color. Allow touch-up paint to dry. Then apply three coats of grid repair compound, allowing three to five minutes drying time between coats. The coating of grid repair compound must extend at least 6.35 mm
 (1/4 inch) on both sides of break area. 

Allow to dry for five minutes; then remove mask. 

 CAUTION: Be careful not to damage the grid line with the razor blade. Further repairs will be necessary. 

After removing mask, check outside appearance of grid repair. If repair compound is visible above or below grid, this excess should be removed. This can be done by placing a single-edge razor blade on the
 back window glass
parallel to grid and scraping gently toward grid. 

 Curing 

The repair coating will air-dry in approximately one minute and can be energized within three to five minutes. Optimum hardness and adhesion occurs after approximately 24 hours. At that time, the repair area may be cleaned with a mild
 window cleaner.

================================================================================
PAGE 2446
================================================================================
1998 Taurus/Sable

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Grid Wire, Back Window Glass�Method II

Use a rear window defroster service kit to repair pigtail connections and grid line breaks. 

The service kit is available from:

Marketing East Company

#10 Liberty Street

North Andover, Massachusetts 01845

Telephone: (508) 689-9565

Any break in the grid longer than 25 mm (1 inch) cannot be serviced. The back window glass (42006)
 must be replaced. For breaks less than 25 mm (1 inch) long, use
 the following procedure:

 Surface Preparation 

Bring the vehicle inside and warm it to 16°C (60°F) or above.

 CAUTION: Do not use scrapers, sharp instruments or abrasive cleaners on the interior surface of the back window glass as this may cause damage to grid lines. 

Clean entire grid line repair area with Ultra-Clear Spray Glass Cleaner E4AZ-19C507-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M14P5-A to remove all dirt, wax, grease, oil or other foreign matter. It is important that repair area be
 clean and dry.

 Application 

Mark location of break on outside of back window glass.

[FIGURE: N12581A.gif]

Place masking tape (provided in kit) over break in grid wire, aligning holes in masking tape with grid wire.

Prepare service kit two-part epoxy.

Check expiration date of package. If hardener has crystallized, place package in hot water until the hardener softens.

Remove plastic clamp from package separating resin and hardener.

Knead package until resin and hardener are thoroughly mixed.

Cut corner of package to open.

Apply two-part epoxy with stick provided to wire grid through cut-out in masking tape.

[FIGURE: N12582A.gif]

Carefully remove masking tape from grid wire repair area.

 NOTE: Use care while using heat gun around interior trim.

Using Rotunda Heat Gun 107-R0300 or equivalent, heat grid wire repair area for one to two minutes.

[FIGURE: N12583A.gif]

 NOTE: Heated back window is now operational.

Two-part epoxy will thoroughly cure in 24 hours. Start engine, turn heated back window switch and light (18C621)
 on and leave on for five minutes. Inspect grid wire
 repair area.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Lead Window Terminal Service�Method I

 NOTE: There are two methods for repairing terminal separation from glass and/or grid breaks. Method I involves soldering the terminal to the glass and Method II uses an epoxy adhesive. Also, grid line repair procedures are different.

Allow back window glass (42006)
 to warm up to room temperature for thirty to sixty minutes. 

Clean bus bar in area to be repaired using fine steel wool (3/0 to 4/0 grade). 

Restore area where bus bar terminal was originally attached by applying three coats of Rear Window Defroster Repair D8AZ-19562-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESB-M4J58-A. Allow approximately 10 minutes drying time between coats. 

Work as quickly as possible to avoid overheating back window glass
. Tin bus bar with solder in area where terminal will be reattached. 

Using Rotunda Heat Gun 107-R0300 or equivalent, preheat back window glass
 in the solder area to 67°-83°C (120°-150°F) just prior to
 soldering terminal on. 

Position terminal on bus bar in area that was tinned and hold it in place with an ice pick or screwdriver. 

[FIGURE: L2447F.gif]

 CAUTION: To avoid damaging bus bar, remove soldering gun or iron as soon as the solder flows. 

Apply soldering heat to pad of terminal until solder flows. 

Start the vehicle, turn heated back window switch and light on, and leave it on for five minutes. Inspect terminal and apply Rear Window Defroster Repair D8AZ-19562-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESB-M4J58-A to the required area.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Instrument Panel

 Lock Cylinder Repair 

Individual lock cylinders are repaired by discarding the inoperative cylinder and building a new lock cylinder using the 
appropriate lock repair package. The lock repair package includes a detailed instruction sheet to build the new lock cylinder 
to 
the current key code of the vehicle.

The instrument panel (04320) features a separate instrument panel reinforcement (04545)
 and houses the controls for most of the vehicle's electrical systems.

The RH side of the instrument panel contains:

the glove compartment (06010).

the passenger side air bag module (044A74).

The center of the instrument panel supports the integrated control panel which contains controls for the audio and temperature control systems. 

The LH side of the instrument panel frames the steering column tube (3514)
 and houses:

the instrument cluster (10849).

the instrument panel finish panel (044D70). 

The instrument panel reinforcement is serviced as part of the instrument panel
 and is not available separately.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Cigar Lighter and Ash Receptacle

An ash receptacle (30702)
 and cigar lighter knob and element (15052)
 are located in the instrument panel (04320)
 (column shift) or console panel (045A36)
 (floor shift).

The cigar lighter knob and element
 has a low-resistance heating coil 
which operates much like the coil used in a portable heater.

When the cigar lighter knob and element
 is pushed completely into the cigar lighter socket and retainer (15055)
, the circuit is closed and current flows through the heating coil to the ground. 

When sufficient heat is generated, the cigar lighter knob and element
 overcomes the spring pressure of the 
bimetal retaining fingers and is released.

SERVICE PRECAUTIONS

Live Air Bags

 WARNING: SAFE HANDLING OF AIR BAG MODULES REQUIRES FOLLOWING THE PROCEDURES DESCRIBED BELOW FOR BOTH LIVE AND DEPLOYED AIR BAGS. 

 ALWAYS WEAR SAFETY GLASSES WHEN SERVICING AN AIR BAG VEHICLE, AND WHEN HANDLING AN AIR BAG. 

 WHEN CARRYING A LIVE AIR BAG, MAKE SURE THE BAG AND TRIM COVER ARE POINTED AWAY FROM YOUR BODY. IN THE UNLIKELY 
EVENT OF AN ACCIDENTAL DEPLOYMENT, THE BAG WILL THEN DEPLOY WITH MINIMAL CHANCE OF INJURY. 

 IN ADDITION, WHEN PLACING A LIVE AIR BAG ON A BENCH OR OTHER SURFACES, ALWAYS FACE THE BAG AND TRIM COVER UP, 
AWAY FROM THE SURFACE. THIS WILL REDUCE THE MOTION OF THE MODULE IF IT IS ACCIDENTALLY DEPLOYED.

================================================================================
PAGE 2456
================================================================================
1998 Taurus/Sable

Section 01-12: Instrument Panel

1998 Taurus, Sable Workshop Manual

SERVICE PRECAUTIONS

Deployed Air Bags

 SAFETY PRECAUTIONS MUST ALSO BE OBSERVED WHEN HANDLING A DEPLOYED AIR BAG. 

 AFTER DEPLOYMENT, THE AIR BAG SURFACE MAY CONTAIN DEPOSITS OF SODIUM HYDROXIDE, A PRODUCT OF THE GAS GENERANT 
COMBUSTION THAT IS IRRITATING TO THE SKIN. 

 ALWAYS WEAR GLOVES AND SAFETY GLASSES WHEN HANDLING A DEPLOYED AIR BAG. 

 WASH YOUR HANDS WITH MILD SOAP AND WATER AFTERWARDS.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Door Locks

 Lock Cylinder Repair 

Individual lock cylinders are repaired by discarding the inoperative cylinder and building a new lock cylinder using the 
appropriate lock repair package. The lock repair package includes a detailed instruction sheet to build the new lock cylinder 
to the current key code of the vehicle.

 Manual 

The manual door lock system consists of:

RH door latch remote control assembly (21818) (inside door handle)

LH door latch remote control assembly (21819) (inside door handle)

RH front door outside handle latch rod (264A64)

LH front door outside handle latch rod (264A65)

door latch cable (221A00) (from inside door handle to latch)

RH front door latch (21812)

LH front door latch (21813)

RH rear door latch (26412)

LH rear door latch (26413)

RH front door pushbutton rod (218A00)

LH front door pushbutton rod (218A01)

RH front door key cylinder rod (22134)

LH front door key cylinder rod (22135)

RH door cable watershield (221A06)

LH door cable watershield (221A07)

RH door ajar switch (14018)

LH door ajar switch (14019)

RH rear door outside handle latch rod (264A00) (from outside door handle)

LH rear door outside handle latch rod (264A01) (from outside door handle)

RH rear door latch lever actuator rod (264A54) (from latch)

LH rear door latch lever actuator rod (264A55) (from latch)

RH rear door link rod (26408) (long rod)

LH rear door link rod (26409) (long rod)

RH rear door bellcrank (26478)

LH rear door bellcrank (26479)

RH rear door pushbutton rod (264A80)

LH rear door pushbutton rod (264A81)

RH door latch actuator (optional with power door locks) (218B20)

LH door latch actuator (optional with power door locks) (218B21)

The doors can be opened by either:

the inside door handle on the door trim panel.

the outside door handle on the door. 

The door handle is connected to the door latch by a door latch remote control (cable).

The front outside door handle is connected to the door latch by an outside handle latch rod, and when unlocked, can be 
opened by pulling on the outside door handle.

The rear outside door handle is connected to an outside handle latch rod which connects to a latch lever actuator rod at 
the latch.

The doors can be locked by:

pushing down on the door latch pushbutton knob.

using the door lock cylinder key (front door only).

The front door can be unlocked by:

pushing up on the door latch pushbutton.

pulling on the inside door handle.

using the door lock cylinder key.

The rear door can only be unlocked by pulling up on the door latch pushbutton knob.

The door latch closes over the door latch striker to keep the door closed. The door latch striker is adjustable.

 Power Door Locks 

 NOTE: If the key is left in either the driver's or passenger's lock cylinder in the lock or unlock position for a period of 
time, it may cause the locks to cycle. This is due to a protective feature in the door lock actuator and is not harmful to the 
lock system. Remove the key and the actuators will function normally.

The power door lock system consists of the components used in the manual door lock system in addition to the following:

front door lock switches (14017) in the door trim panel arm rests

RH door latch actuator (adjunct)(218B20), LH door latch actuator (adjunct)(218B21), rear door (liftgate) electric latch 
actuator (linear)(26594)

circuit wiring and circuit protection

lock and unlock relays 

optional driver's, passenger's and liftgate key cylinder switches

When the raised portion of either front door lock switch
 is pressed, ground is supplied to the all door lock relay and all doors lock.

The driver door will be kept from locking by the generic electronic module (GEM) if the following inputs are present:

driver door ajar

key-in-ignition signal present

lock sense command

When the depressed portion of either front door lock switch
 is pressed, ground is supplied to the all door unlock relay and driver's door unlock relay and all doors unlock.

Vehicles equipped with Perimeter Anti-Theft System also have GEM controlled central locking. This system allows driver's 
door to be unlocked or all doors to be unlocked using door key cylinder switches.

To operate central locking unlock functions:

Turn key in door lock cylinder to unlock position. The door will unlock mechanically.

Turn same lock cylinder to unlock within five seconds and all doors unlock.

Turn either door key cylinder to lock and all doors will lock.

For station wagons, liftgate lock cylinder switch will unlock all doors, but will not lock.

 Lock Cylinder Service 

Individual lock cylinders are serviced by discarding the inoperative lock cylinder and building a new lock cylinder using 
the appropriate lock service package. The lock service package includes a detailed instruction sheet to build the new lock 
cylinder to the current key code of the vehicle.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Lock, Child Safety

The child safety lock:

when activated, prevents the rear door (24630)
 from being opened from inside the vehicle regardless of the position of the rear door latch push button rod (26460)
.

has been designed into the rear door latches (26412). A bezel on the rear door
 shows the location of the lever.

does not lock the rear door from the outside. It is still necessary to push the rear door latch push button rod
 down to lock the rear door
 from outside.

The rear door latch lever is manually moved up to lock and down to unlock the child safety lock system.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Latch, Liftgate

The liftgate latch is not adjustable. All adjustments are made to the liftgate/luggage compartment latch striker (404A42)
.

The liftgate latch has a two-stage latching mechanism. The first stage holds the liftgate closed, but does not hold it 
tight against the weatherstrips and seals. This may be called the secondary position.

This position will not open the switch that generates the "Liftgate Ajar" signal.

The second stage seals the liftgate against wind noise and water leaks. This may be called the primary position. This 
position also opens the switch that generates the "Liftgate Ajar" signal.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Handles, Locks, Latches and Mechanisms

Refer to Electrical and Vacuum Troubleshooting Manual, Cell 59 , Generic Electronic Module for schematic and connector information. 

Refer to Electrical and Vacuum Troubleshooting Manual, Cell 110 , Power Door Locks for schematic and connector information. 

Refer to Electrical and Vacuum Troubleshooting Manual, Cell 113 , Trunk Lid Release for schematic and connector information. 

 Inspection and Verification 

Verify the customer concern by operating the power door locks and liftgate or luggage compartment door remote release to 
duplicate the condition.

Inspect to determine if one of the following mechanical or electrical concerns apply:

 VISUAL INSPECTION CHART

Mechanical

Electrical

Door alignment.

Latch damage.

Latch binding.

Failed Power Distribution Circuit Breaker 4 (30A).

Failed fuse junction panel Fuse 23 (5A), Fuse 12 (5A), Fuse 26 (15A).

Corroded connectors.

Loose connectors.

If inspection reveals an obvious concern that is readily identified, service as required. Correct the concern before 
continuing with Inspection and Verification.

If the concern remains after the inspection, connect the Rotunda New Generation STAR (NGS) Tester 418-F048 (007-00500) or 
equivalent to the data link connector (DLC) located beneath the instrument panel and select the vehicle to be tested from the 
NGS menu. If the NGS does not communicate with the vehicle:

check that program card is properly installed.

check connections to vehicle.

check ignition switch position.

If the NGS still does not communicate with the vehicle, refer to the New Generation STAR (NGS) Tester manual.

Perform DATA LINK DIAGNOSTIC TEST using the NGS. If the NGS responds with:

CKT 70 = ALL MODULES NO RESPONSE/NOT EQUIPPED, go to Communication System Diagnostics in Section 18-04 to diagnose 
network concern.

NO RESPONSE/NOT EQUIPPED for generic electronic module (GEM), go to Pinpoint Test A.

SYSTEM PASSED for the GEM, retrieve and record continuous diagnostic trouble codes (DTCs), erase continuous DTCs, then 
execute Self Test Diagnostics for the GEM.

If DTCs retrieved are related to the concern, go to the Generic Electronic Module (GEM) Diagnostic Trouble Code (DTC) 
Index to continue diagnostics.

If no DTCs related to the concern are retrieved, go to the Symptom Chart to continue diagnostics.

Rotunda Service Bay Diagnostic System (SBDS®) 418-F001 (001-00001) may also be used to diagnose this system.

 GENERIC ELECTRONIC MODULE (GEM) DIAGNOSTIC TROUBLE CODES (DTCS) INDEX

DTC

Description

Action to Take

B1302

Delayed Accessory Relay Coil Circuit Failure

GO to Section 01-11 .

B1304

Delayed Accessory Relay Coil Circuit Short to Battery

GO to Section 01-11 .

B1309

All Door Lock Sense Circuit Short to Ground

GO to DTC B1309.

B1310

Power Door Unlock Circuit Failure

GO to DTC B1310.

B1314

Battery Saver Relay Coil Circuit Open

GO to Section 17-02 .

B1315

Battery Saver Relay Coil Circuit Short to Battery

Remove front door latch (with pushbutton rod and key cylinder rod attached) from front door cavity.

 door ajar switch clockwise (for RH door latch) or counterclockwise (for LH door latch) until switch releases. Remove

as necessary.

 CAUTION: Do not drive out the center of the bellcrank rivet, or the door sheet metal may be damaged. Drill the rivet or cut the 
head of the rivet to remove it.

Remove rear door latch control rod retainer (220A48) from door by twisting with a flat-blade screwdriver.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Actuator, Power Door Lock

 Removal 

Position window glass in the up position.

Remove the front or rear door latch assembly as described.

Remove RH or LH door ajar switch from the door latch as described.

[FIGURE: AN1971A.gif]

Using a flat-blade screwdriver, gently pry up the locking tab and slide the adjunct power door latch actuator off the 
door latch.

[FIGURE: AN1972A.gif]

[FIGURE: AN1975A.gif]

 Installation 

 NOTE: The adjunct power door latch actuator must be installed BEFORE the door ajar switch is installed.

Engage one end of the adjunct power door latch actuator to the channel on the door latch.

Press down on actuator to engage the other end of the actuator to its channel on the door latch.

Slide the actuator onto the door latch, while making sure that the pin on the actuator engages through the yellow bushing 
on the arm of the latch properly, until actuator clicks into place.

Follow front or rear door latch removal procedure in reverse order. Tighten door latch retaining screws to 10-14 
Nm (89-123 lb-in).

 Liftgate 

 Removal 

Open liftgate (40010).

Remove liftgate inside trim panel. Refer to Section 01-05 .

Remove 12 nuts retaining rear reflector and socket to liftgate
. Remove rear reflector and socket. Refer to Section 17-01 .

[FIGURE: AN0635B.gif]

.

 Liftgate Lock Cylinder 

[FIGURE: AN0096D.gif]

.

[FIGURE: AN0152A.gif]

.

 Liftgate Latch Assembly 

[FIGURE: N12982A.gif]

 by twisting one-quarter turn and lifting bulb and socket out of rear license plate housing and bracket.

.

Remove three nuts retaining rear license plate housing and bracket
to liftgate
. 

 Rear License Plate Housing and Bracket Assembly 

[FIGURE: AN0160A.gif]

Remove three retaining nuts and remove actuator mounting bracket from rear license plate housing and bracket
.

 Installation

to 3-4 Nm (27-35 lb-in).

Section 01-14B: Door Lock Control System, Electronic

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Door Lock Control System, Electronic

The electronic door lock control system has three main components:

remote anti-theft personality (RAP) module with internal antenna, located underneath instrument panel (04320) to the right of the steering column 

five-button keyless entry keypad (14A626) on the driver door (optional on GL, GS and Wagon)

four-button (hand-held) keyless entry remote transmitter (15K601)

The door locks are controlled by the RAP module through the use of external relays.

The remote anti-theft personality module uses a rolling code strategy to decrease the potential for unauthorized use. The 
remote entry transmitter has a counter that must match, or be synchronized with the vehicle's remote entry receiver's counter 
in order for the system to operate. It is possible for the transmitter's rolling code counter to become de-synchronized with 
the vehicle receiver's counter. In this event, a diagnostic trouble code should be stored. Refer to the appropriate DTC 
Index(es). In addition, this module controls the perimeter anti-theft system; refer to Section 13-11A .

The door locks are wired so that the lock and unlock switches on the doors/liftgate can operate the door locks with or 
without a RAP module installed in the system. The door lock switches are wired directly to the relays that control the door 
locks.

When the RAP module operates the door locks, it provides a ground, similar to the door lock switches. 

Operating through the RAP module, the electronic door lock control system performs the following functions when using the keyless entry remote transmitter
:

unlocks driver door

unlocks all doors and liftgate

locks all doors and liftgate

opens luggage compartment door

panic alarm

issues interior lamps on (when unlocking) and off commands (when locking) to the generic electronic module (GEM)

horn chirp verifies when LOCK on keyless entry remote transmitter is pressed twice

double horn chirp notifies when door left open

deactivates a triggered perimeter alarm

arms/disarms anti-theft system

allows up to four keyless entry remote transmitters to be programmed

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Inputs and Outputs

The remote anti-theft personality (RAP) module receives input from the following for the electrical door lock system:

keyless entry remote transmitters (15K601)

keyless entry keypad (14A626)

door disarm switches (left, right and liftgate lock cylinders)

door ajar output from generic electronic module (GEM)

door lock switches (left, right and liftgate)

door unlock switches (left, right and liftgate)

stoplamp switch

transmission range (TR) sensor

ignition switch

The RAP module distributes output to the following for the electronic door lock system:

driver door unlock relay

all doors unlock relay

lock all doors relay

luggage compartment door release relay

horn relay

headlamp relay

illuminated entry request output to GEM

keypad lamp

theft indicator in instrument cluster (if equipped)

liftgate door unlock relay (wagon)

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Entry Code

The system (permanent) entry code is located in three places:

on the owner's wallet code card (in glove compartment)

electronically accessible by requesting the remote anti-theft personality (RAP) module KEYCODE PID on the New Generation 
Star (NGS) Tester 418-F048 (007-00500) or equivalent.

on the RAP module housing

The RAP module is programmed at the factory with a five-digit entry code. A replacement RAP module includes replacement 
labels and a new owner's code card.

To turn on the interior lamps and light all illuminated components:

press any button on the keyless entry keypad (14A626).

To program a temporary access code:

Enter the permanent code on the keyless entry keypad.

Press button 1/2 within 5 seconds of last digit of permanent code. (This alerts system to accept temporary code.)

Enter alternate five-digit code. Do not exceed 5 seconds between entering digits or between pressing the 1/2 key and 
entering the first digit.

Section 01-14B: Door Lock Control System, Electronic

1998 Taurus, Sable Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Keyless Entry Keypad

The keyless entry keypad is located on the driver door and performs the following functions:

unlocks driver door

unlocks all doors and liftgate

locks all doors and liftgate

releases luggage compartment door

lights keypad lamp

deactivates a triggered perimeter alarm (refer to Section 13-11A )

arm/disarm anti-theft system (refer to Section 13-11A )

allows one user code to be programmed

issues interior lamps on (when unlocking) and off commands (when locking) to the generic electronic module (GEM)

 Keyless Entry Keypad 

[FIGURE: N13281A.gif]

To lock all doors and liftgate:

press the 7/8 and 9/0 buttons at the same time. (It is not necessary to enter the key code first.)

This will turn off courtesy lamps and prearm the anti-theft alarm system.

To unlock the driver door, and disarm the anti-theft alarm control, if equipped:

Enter the permanent factory code or enter the owner's alternate code.

To unlock the passenger door(s) and liftgate:

press the 3/4 button within five seconds of unlocking the driver door or luggage compartment door.

The remote anti-theft personality (RAP) module has the ability to recognize one factory keyless entry code and one 
user-programmed keyless entry code. 

The factory code will be programmed at the manufacturing plant and stored in non-volatile memory. 

The user-programmed keyless entry code will be programmed by the user and will be stored in non-volatile memory. 

The keyless entry code will be input by the user as a series of five keys input from the keypad. 

The keyless entry keypad functions as follows: 

Upon reading a valid key, the module will respond in the following manner:

Store the key in memory keycode. 

Activate the keypad lamp for five seconds. 

Issue an interior lamp on request to the GEM. 

Upon reading five sequential keys, the module will check the code against both the factory keyless code and the user 
programmed keyless code. 

If a match exists, between what the user has input at the keypad and the codes stored in memory, the module will respond 
by activating the driver door unlock output and disarming the anti-theft system. A key read is considered to be sequential if 
the valid key is read within five seconds of the last valid key read. If more than five seconds has gone by, i.e. the keypad 
lamp has timed out, the user must start over at the beginning of the keypad code sequence.

1998 Taurus/Sable

Section 01-14B: Door Lock Control System, Electronic

1998 Taurus, Sable Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Autolock

All doors will automatically lock each time the vehicle is driven after all the following steps are completed.

Ignition switch is in RUN/ACC and the autolock feature is enabled (refer to Enabling and Disabling as described).

The reverse lamp switch is activated (passing either into or out of REVERSE).

All doors and the luggage compartment/liftgate are closed when the driver releases the brake.

 NOTE: The door ajar state is monitored continuously for 500ms after an autolock has occurred. If a door is opened again within 
this time, the driver door will unlock.

After this initial lock, all doors will automatically relock when any door is opened and then closed followed by the 
driver releasing the brake pedal. However, the doors will not relock if the ignition switch is OFF.

The same feature as described in the note above applies to a relock also.

The door may not automatically lock if the driver:

shifts the transmission into gear without pressing the brake pedal.

shifts the transmission quickly into gear after starting the engine.

releases the brake pedal and presses the accelerator pedal before a door is closed.

 Enabling and Disabling 

To enable (or disable) the autolock feature, use the following steps or 
use the enabling and disabling features sequence as described.

Enter the five-digit permanent entry code into the keyless entry keypad (14A626).

Within five seconds of entering the code, press and hold the 7/8 button on the keypad.

Within five seconds of Step 2, and while holding the 7/8 button, press the 3/4 button on the keypad and release it.

Within five seconds of Step 3, release the 7/8 button on the keypad.

If the autolock feature is disabled, the horn will chirp once. If the autolock feature is enabled, the horn will chirp 
once shortly and then a second time with a longer honk when the sequence is completed.

If vehicle is not equipped with keyless entry keypad, the autolock/relock feature can also be 
disabled and enabled as follows:

Make sure the anti-theft system is not armed or triggered, ignition is OFF and all doors and liftgate are closed.

Turn the ignition switch from OFF to RUN.

Press the door power unlock button 3 times.

Turn the ignition switch from RUN to OFF.

Press the door power unlock button 3 times.

Turn the ignition switch back to RUN within 30 seconds of step 2.

The horn should chirp once. If not, wait 30 seconds and repeat steps 1 through 6.

Press the door power unlock button.

Press the door power lock button.

The horn will chirp once if the Autolock feature was deactivated, twice (one short chirp followed by a long chirp) if the 
Autolock feature was activated.

Turn the ignition switch OFF.

The horn will chirp once to confirm that you activated or deactivated the Autolock feature.

The New Generation STAR NGS configuration function card can also be used to enable/disable the autolock feature.

1998 Taurus, Sable Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Transmitter, Keyless Entry Remote

 NOTE: The remote entry features will not function when the ignition switch is in the RUN or ACC position.

The keyless entry remote transmitter (15K601) performs the following functions:

unlocks driver door

unlocks all doors and liftgate

releases luggage compartment door

operates personal security alarm (refer to Section 13-11A )

arms/disarms anti-theft system (refer to Section 13-11A )

issues interior lamps on (when unlocking) and off (when locking) commands to the generic electronic module (GEM)

The electronic door lock control system includes two four-button (hand-held) keyless entry remote transmitters. Keyless entry remote transmitters
 are reprogrammable and all keyless entry remote transmitters
 for the vehicle must be set at the same time. When troubleshooting the system, one keyless entry remote transmitter
 is essential to perform tests.

To unlock the driver door:

Press the unlock button on the keyless entry remote transmitter. 

This will also disarm the anti-theft system.

To unlock all doors and liftgate:

Press the unlock button on the keyless entry remote transmitter a second time, within five 
seconds of the first unlock.

 NOTE: If more than five seconds have elapsed since the first press of the unlock button, pressing the unlock button again will 
only unlock the driver door a second time.

To lock all doors and arm the anti-theft system (if equipped):

press lock button on the keyless entry remote transmitter once.

To confirm that the doors have locked (and that the anti-theft system has armed):

press lock button again, from one to five seconds after the first press. The horn will chirp once if the doors have been 
locked and all doors and the liftgate are closed. The horn will chirp twice if one of the doors or liftgate are open. 

To activate the personal security alarm:

press the red panic button on any keyless entry remote transmitter
. The horn will beep and the headlamps and exterior lamps will flash for a maximum of two minutes and 45 seconds.

To deactivate the personal security alarm:

press the red panic button again on any keyless entry remote transmitter or turn the ignition switch to 
RUN.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Programming, Electronic Door Lock Control System

 NOTE: Keyless entry remote transmitters (15K601) have individual codes and adding a new code erases a previous code. There is no sure way to determine which code is 
erased.

When the customer has purchased additional keyless entry remote transmitters, or has replaced a lost keyless entry remote transmitter
, the customer MUST bring to the dealer ALL keyless entry remote transmitters
 for the vehicle. 

The dealer must then reprogram ALL keyless entry remote transmitters at the same time. 

The remote anti-theft personality (RAP) module erases all previous keyless entry remote transmitters from memory when the keyless entry remote transmitters
 are programmed or reprogrammed. 

The RAP module can store up to four keyless entry remote transmitters in memory.

 NOTE: Be aware that when in program mode, any transmitter pressed within 30 meters of the vehicle may get programmed to that 
vehicle (thus erasing all of the codes).

To program (or reprogram) keyless entry remote transmitters into the RAP module, perform the 
following steps.

Make sure that the anti-theft system is not armed or triggered. Refer to Section 13-11A . 

Turn the ignition switch from OFF to RUN eight times within 10 seconds, ending in RUN.

Program mode can also be entered if the ignition switch is cycled from OFF to START four times within 10 seconds, ending 
in RUN.

If the RAP module has successfully entered program mode, it will lock and then unlock all doors.

Press any button on a keyless entry remote transmitter within 20 seconds of step 2 and 
the doors will lock and then unlock to confirm that each keyless entry remote transmitter has been programmed. 

If the door locks do not respond for any keyless entry remote transmitter
, wait a few seconds and press the button again. If the door locks still fail to respond, go to Diagnosis and Testing, Pinpoint 
Test D.

Turn ignition switch OFF (or wait up to twenty seconds after Step 2) to exit program mode. If a new set of keyless entry remote transmitters
 have been programmed (or reprogrammed), the RAP module will lock and unlock all doors one last time to confirm.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Security Mode Operation

The remote anti-theft personality (RAP) module also controls the panic mode functions. 

Upon activation of the panic mode by pressing the keyless entry remote transmitter panic button, the RAP module sends a 
signal to activate the horn (13832), headlamps and exterior lamps for approximately two minutes and 45 seconds. 

The RAP module cancels the panic alarm if the panic button is pressed again or if the ignition switch is turned to the 
RUN or ACC position.
